mine.text: Record myself playing along with the backing track

suggestions.text: Undo: a list of steps to jump back through; marks for clip, chop, guitar and tempo steps; ghosts of the notes an Undo took away
Take out / insert bars for the whole song at once (the chart, every lane, the takes): Logic's cut and insert time, its own design
Virtuals, next: move the picked bars, paste an octave down (melody onto the bass), pick bars across several lanes, Repeat ×n
Virtuals on a real iPhone: tap bars on a part's lane, Repeat, Copy then Paste onto another lane, Take out, and Undo's caption and marks
Video: takes follow the tempo (sound stretched with the pitch kept, film at the matching speed); first measure four stretchers at once on an iPhone
Video: record an A/V take on a real iPhone (camera, preview, the film lined up, size per minute), and play four lanes at a changed tempo: can its audio thread keep up?
Video: film with an iPhone as the Mac's camera (Continuity Camera): pick it, record, and see how late its picture is
Video: Earlier / Later for a take's picture (a camera's own delay)
Video: frame each film in its tile (zoom, move) on a real iPhone with fingers; the export must use the same framing (framing.js filmRect)
Line up recordings made outside the app (a phone's camera, a bandmate's file) by a clap on the count-in
Video: films in a shared song file, and one finished 1080×1920 reel of the tiles to export (WebCodecs + a small MP4 muxer)
Endings: listen to G~ and G! (try |C|G|D7,G~|), then: show the hit on the chord strip, a longer ring-out at the very end
Strum editor: a row of tappable strokes per beat group (boom, strum, full, mute, miss) for guitar and mando, saved beside the song; same characters as strumPatterns.js

The chart editor's Buttons way is hidden for now (OFFER_BUTTONS in ArrangementEditor): say what it needs, then bring it back. Ideas: drag bars to reorder, keys mid-song, slash chords, arrow keys on a Mac
The bar playing lit in the chart's text (Transcribe, Arranger, Tracks): try it on iPhone with the keypad up
Piano roll on a real iPad and iPhone: swipe scrolls, tap picks, drag the picked note or its length handle, the note bar's steps. Then: scroll the roll when a dragged note nears its edge?
Transcribe's pencil: should its Melody tab open on ABC (the roll is already on the page)?
Tracks: audio editing (trim, split, delete, move, level, fades, comping takes, Undo) and the tempo lane
Tracks: try clip editing on a real iPhone (picking, grips, fade squares, the clip tools in the control bar) and by ear
Tracks: crossfade where two clips meet, and copy / paste a clip
Tracks: change where a chord starts in the bar (a box per beat, like Transcribe's Band lane), and add or remove one
Tracks: chord lanes follow the chord display (shapes, concert, Roman, Nashville)
The tune's chord symbols follow chord edits in the chart (now they stay as written, so the sheet music can show old chords)
Tracks: try the part editor on a real iPhone (pane under the lanes, or a full-screen sheet with Done?)
Tracks on a phone: narrower lane headers so the lanes have room
Tracks: step a bar back or on, like Transcribe (the cycle is there now)
One track-grid look for Transcribe and Tracks (header, ruler, control bar shared)
Guess the chords: score it against your own finished transcriptions, and tune it on them
Guess where bar 1 goes (chord changes land on bar lines with the bass on the root), so the slide is suggested
Chords learned from everyone's transcriptions (needs the backend, consent, many songs)
MIDI file: the tempo lane as a tempo track, so a ritard reaches Logic
Takes: ask the browser to protect them (persist), keep the take in use + last few, offer to clear the rest
Takes saved as 24-bit FLAC (hand-written encoder, browsers already play it): about half the size, lossless
Stems: render each stem in its own pass, WAV it and let go before the next, so a long song fits an iPhone
Limits: songs live in localStorage (5 MB cap); move them to IndexedDB behind storage/
Limits: beat finding freezes the page 1–2 s; move it to a Web Worker
Limits: measure on an iPhone: the slow-downer's CPU, and a new player per note during playback
Tests with Vitest for the song logic (chart, bass, MIDI, theory)
Transcribe: keep the tune, chords and markers on their bars when a bar is fixed
Check the beat finder against Logic's tempo maps
Transcribe: suggest the song's key from the recording (Find already fits the notes to string-band keys); you accept it, it never overwrites yours
Transcribe: slide and trim the recording on a phone (bigger grips, pinch to zoom)
Transcribe: fixes that stick (pins the beat finder must pass through), which also handle ritards
Transcribe: the parts on their own instruments, key change; pinch to zoom
Chord tutor: tensions and avoid notes, extensions (9, ♭9), and harmony parts using the same scale choice
Tap a note in the sheet music to play from there
Speed trainer: loop gets a little faster each pass
Slow down or change key without changing the other (Amazing Slow Downer style)
Latency calibration so recordings line up with the band
Recorded takes in the exported mix and stems (render the lanes' clips offline, with their level and fades)
Hear yourself through the app while recording (try it, measure the delay)
Shared projects: songs and takes sync between collaborators (backend)
Hear-it loop: G boom-chuck from an attempt, blind A/B
Strum motion: bluegrass bounce vs pendulum A/B, then Irish on six strings
Band plays my recorded samples from the manifest
Guitar or mandolin tab under the melody (with capo)
Import a MIDI file as the melody, through the piano roll
Swap harmony options without restarting the band
Hum or sing a tune into the mic and get it written as ABC
Lyric chart: tap the word where each bar starts, instead of typing |
Light up each syllable as it's sung, on the chart and the sheet music
Read an ABC tune's own words (w: lines) into the chart
Chords that fit: try the suggestions by ear on real songs (On and On), and tune the ranking and blue notes
Harmony locks: lock and unlock bars of a generated line on a real iPhone (the lock on the roll’s ruler is small), and hear a chord change redo only the unlocked bars
Harmony locks for half a bar (where a note crosses the middle, lock the whole bar), and a lock in the TAB and score views
Passing chords in the harmony voices on approach notes, anticipations and suspensions (the Passing chords harmony style)
Mandolin chops for every chord type (now only major and minor), at the bottom of the neck
Chord editors: hear the chord on its own, and use one chord’s changes for every same chord in the song
Fills: hear a note as you draw it, copy a fill to other chords, and place it at the start of a chord
The Guitar lane opens the same diagram editor for its shapes (six strings, boom notes marked)
Chord tutor and harmony parts read the Berklee tables (chordScaleFor) so there's one place for chord scales
Mixolydian tunes as a key (Old Joe Clark): ♭VII in the key, no avoid notes
Passing chords harmony style: try it by ear against the stack (piano roll harmony options)
Voicings that know the melody: a top-note voicing, or which notes to keep from the melody note (one more input to voiceChord)
Harmony: a bass singer part that sings mostly roots (the rare fourth voice in bluegrass vocals)
Harmony: make two parts (lead and tenor) and three parts (tenor above, baritone below) the obvious choices, the bluegrass texture
Harmony layout: melody on top, voices below filling out the chord (jazz soli style), as an option beside the bluegrass stack
